issues.description: PersonService constructor differs between template and solution: the template uses constructor injection `PersonService(PersonRepository personRepository)`, while the solution defines a no-args constructor `PersonService()` that sets `personRepository` to null. This breaks the intended Spring DI setup and will cause NullPointerExceptions when any service method calls `personRepository`.
issues.suggestedFix: In the solution repository, remove the no-args constructor and restore constructor injection: `public PersonService(PersonRepository personRepository) { this.personRepository = personRepository; }` so Spring can wire the repository and runtime NPEs are avoided.

issues.description: The problem statement instructs students to adapt and run a deployment build script (`build.sh` for Linux/Mac or `build.bat` for Windows), but neither file exists in the template or solution repository. This prevents students from locating the referenced artifacts and makes the deployment steps unclear/impossible to follow as written.
issues.suggestedFix: Add `build.sh` and `build.bat` at the repository root containing the commands described in the problem statement (optionally reading the app name from `heroku-app-name.txt`), or update the problem statement to reference the actual script filename(s) that exist in the repository.

issues.description: Mismatch between the problem statement and the solution Dockerfile regarding the suggested executable permission for `start.sh`: the statement suggests `chmod 700 start.sh`, while the solution uses `RUN chmod 770 start.sh`. Both may work, but the differing numeric mode can confuse students who try to match the reference exactly.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the artifacts by changing the solution Dockerfile to `RUN chmod 700 start.sh`, or loosen the problem statement wording to "make start.sh executable (e.g., chmod 700/770/755)".
